The move comes as Canada faces criticism from Donald Trump’s administration over its “unacceptable” efforts to combat forced labour.

Two helicopters collided over Rio de Janeiro on Sunday morning and crashed in the city’s western zone, killing all six people onboard, including Tree, several Brazilian media outlets reported.

guardian.description:
Almost every child, including those from high-income countries, is now exposed to at least one hazard

Half of the world’s children are exposed to at least three overlapping climate hazards threatening their health, education and survival, according to a Unicef report.

Globally, children face increasing threats from heatwaves, storms, floods and droughts as the climate crisis worsens, with more than one billion facing at least three of these at once.

rfi.title: France powers ahead in AI development, with more funding, public service tools
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Tuesday a further investment of €655 million to accelerate the development of artificial intelligence as well as an AI programme for public service employees. France is keen to build strategic autonomy in the face of competition from China and the United States.

rfi.title: G7 summit opens full day of talks with Ukraine, Iran and Trump tensions in focus
rfi.description: As the G7 summit enters its first full day of discussions, French President Emmanuel Macron faces the challenge of keeping his US counterpart Donald Trump engaged as leaders weigh pressure on Russia, Middle East diplomacy and renewed trade tensions with Washington.

rfi.title: Child sexual abuse commission urges France to speed up reforms
rfi.description: Only a third of the recommendations made more than two years ago by France's Independent Commission on Incest and Sexual Violence Against Children (Ciivise) have been fully implemented, the body said in an assessment submitted to the government.

rfi.title: Fearsome France begin World Cup wary of over-confidence
rfi.description: France come into this year's World Cup as one of the leading contenders for the trophy having reached the final of the last two editions, but Tuesday's opponents in their opening game, Senegal, serve as a warning of the dangers of over-confidence.

rfi.title: Former CAR leader Bozizé on trial over crimes against humanity
rfi.description: A UN-backed court in the the Central African Republic will on Tuesday begin the trial in absentia of former president François Bozizé, over crimes against humanity committed between 2009 and 2013.

rfi.title: Journalists disappear as intimidation grips Mozambique's Cabo Delgado region
rfi.description: Almost a decade after an Islamist insurgency erupted in Mozambique's northern Cabo Delgado province, few reports on the conflict are emerging from the region. This third instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – hears from journalists and activists facing intimidation and violence.

rfi.title: France's Macron warns Iran against imposing Hormuz tolls
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday warned Iran against imposing tolls on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, saying "everything" should be done so fees are not charged for passage through the key bottleneck.

rfi.title: US and Iran reach deal to end war, reopen Hormuz
rfi.description: The United States and Iran said they reached a deal to end the Middle East war on all fronts including Lebanon, and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz, but offered little indication on the thorny question of Tehran's nuclear programme.

rfi.title: NGO warns Ebola epidemic is 'outpacing' response efforts in DRC
rfi.description: French NGO Doctors Without Borders warned Monday that "dangerous gaps" remain in efforts to rein in an Ebola outbreak that has killed more than 180 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Since the first reported cases a month ago, the virus has spread rapidly, with the situation now critical in Ituri province.

rfi.title: ‘No blank cheque' for president or government says Senegal’s Sonko
rfi.description: In his first major international interview since becoming Speaker of Senegal's National Assembly, former prime minister Ousmane Sonko talks to RFI and sister channel France 24 about his split with his long-time ally President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. In the wide-reaching discussion, he also touches on the debt crisis, homosexuality legislation, regional security, his political aspirations and the World Cup.

rfi.title: First contact: Cape Verde's rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Cape Verde will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the third instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the second smallest nation after Curaçao to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: Macron leads effort to bridge divides with Trump at France's G7 summit
rfi.description: As a G7 summit opens in eastern France on Monday, President Emmanuel Macron is set to lead the allies' efforts to narrow differences with the United States on Iran, Ukraine, trade and big tech regulation.

rfi.title: Cameroon opposition figure files complaint in France against President Biya
rfi.description: Former Cameroonian presidential candidate Issa Tchiroma Bakary says he's filed two complaints with the Paris Judicial Court against President Paul Biya, citing the principle of universal jurisdiction.

rfi.title: Clashes as thousands protest in Geneva ahead of G7 summit in France
rfi.description: Protesters in Geneva threw stones and firecrackers at the police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons during a demonstration Sunday against the G7 summit in nearby Evian.

rfi.title: Somaliland president makes 'historic' visit to Israel
rfi.description: Somaliland's President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi met his Israeli counterpart on Sunday in Jerusalem in his first-ever state visit, which comes months after Israel officially recognised the breakaway African state.

rfi.title: UK intercepts Russian shadow fleet vessel in Channel: ministry
rfi.description: British forces on Sunday intercepted a sanctioned oil tanker belonging to Russia's shadow fleet in the English Channel, the defence ministry said, in a six-hour operation hailed by Kyiv.

rfi.title: The project nurturing West Africa's new generation of women filmmakers
rfi.description: Some of the West African film industry's biggest names are backing a new mentorship programme to support emerging women filmmakers. Showcased at this year's Cannes Film Festival, the Mariama Lab project aims to help women bring their stories to a wider audience in the region and beyond.

rfi.title: Ghana lodges protest over Canada's refusal to admit rape case suspect Partey
rfi.description: Ghana's government confirmed on Saturday it had lodged a formal protest with Canada over its refusal to issue an entry visa to the Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey ahead of Ghana's game against Panama on Wednesday in Toronto.

euronews.title: SpaceX buys AI coding startup Cursor for $60bn as AI race with OpenAI and Anthropic intensifies
euronews.description: SpaceX has agreed to acquire Anysphere, the company behind the popular AI coding tool Cursor, in an all-stock deal valuing the startup at $60 billion (€51.7bn), just days after Elon Musk's firm had a record-breaking IPO.

euronews.title: Who is Pico Lopes, the unlikely Cape Verde World Cup hero recruited through LinkedIn?
euronews.description: The national team's call came from 4,500 km away across the Ocean and not in the way most people would expect.

euronews.title: London West End's Shaftesbury Theatre to be renamed to honour Judi Dench
euronews.description: The name change of one of the West End’s most iconic stages celebrates one of the greatest British performers. Dame Judi Dench has been left “truly overwhelmed” by the news.

euronews.title: Investors look beyond the 'Magnificent 7' as Wall Street embraces the 'FAB 10'
euronews.description: SpaceX's record-breaking market debut has pushed Wall Street to widen its favourite shorthand of the so-called 'Magnificent 7', with strategists folding Elon Musk's firm, OpenAI and Anthropic into a new 'FAB 10' label that captures the next phase of the AI trade.

euronews.title: Rolls-Royce secures deal to build small nuclear reactors for Sweden
euronews.description: Rolls-Royce SMR has won a "multi-billion pound" contract to build three small modular nuclear reactors for Sweden, marking a major step in the British engineering group's ambition to become a leading supplier of the technology in Europe.

euronews.title: Russian Tu-22M3 bomber crashes during training flight
euronews.description: Russian Tu-22M3 strategic bomber has crashed in the Irkutsk region during a training flight, amid reports of engine failure. The Defence Ministry said it was not carrying weapons and the crew ejected safely. Four people were taken to hospital.

euronews.title: Trump tells Netanyahu 'be responsible with Lebanon, let Syria handle Hezbollah' at G7
euronews.description: Trump questions Netanyahu's methods, says Beirut strike was excessive, and points to Syria’s President as the most “capable” of countering Hezbollah.

euronews.title: Watch: German chancellor surprises Trump with 'Trump 47' football jersey at G7
euronews.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz presented U.S. President Donald Trump with a personalized football jersey during the G7 summit in France.

euronews.title: MEPs approve EU-US trade deal despite Trump’s new trade war threats
euronews.description: The agreement removes EU tariffs on US goods while accepting a 15 percent levy in the other direction.

euronews.title: Education: Where in the EU has the most early school dropouts?
euronews.description: The number of young Europeans leaving education early is falling, but geography and employment prospects still shape the picture. How do EU countries compare with each other?

euronews.title: Humanoid robots join models at fashion show in Seoul
euronews.description: Humanoid robots wearing designer outfits shared the runway with human models at a futuristic fashion show in Seoul, highlighting advances in robotics and AI.

euronews.title: Deadline looms for UniCredit's hostile bid for Commerzbank
euronews.description: Tuesday marks the final day for UniCredit's hostile and highly political takeover offer for Commerzbank, as Italy's second-largest bank has its sights on an ambitious pan-European banking merger.

euronews.title: Moscow oil refinery ablaze after retaliatory Ukrainian drone strike
euronews.description: Kyiv claimed the attack as retaliation for Russia's intensifying aerial campaign, a day after drones damaged a UNESCO-listed monastery complex in the capital.

euronews.title: Anish Kapoor brings darkness, mirrors and the 'sublime' to London’s Hayward Gallery
euronews.description: A major new exhibition showcasing the work of Turner Prize-winner Anish Kapoor has opened at London’s Hayward Gallery, bringing together blood-red suspended sculptures, distorted mirror installations and void-like forms that warp perception and space.

euronews.title: Nvidia raises over €21.5bn in first bond sale since 2021 as AI growth race continues
euronews.description: Nvidia has returned to the corporate debt market for the first time in five years, pricing a $25 billion (€21.5bn) bond sale that drew roughly $85 billion (€73.2bn) in orders, a sign of investors' strong appetite for exposure to AI.

euronews.title: Ships start to trickle through Strait of Hormuz, but who will run it still in doubt
euronews.description: Trump said the strait would be "completely open" by Friday, but key details over who will manage the crucial waterway remain unresolved. Meanwhile, Iran has made further claims that it will control Hormuz in the future based on its interpretation of the framework deal with the US.

euronews.title: Rare first edition of ‘Wuthering Heights’ (complete with spelling mistakes) to go up for auction
euronews.description: It’s the first copy of the Gothic novel in the publisher’s original cloth binding to be auctioned since 1908.

lemonde.title: Violences faites aux mineurs : immersion au parquet de Béthune, entre « masse » de dossiers au quotidien et mort de Lyhanna
lemonde.description: Le procureur de la République et son équipe ont accepté d’ouvrir leurs portes au « Monde ». De la permanence téléphonique où arrivent les appels des commissariats à celle qui réceptionne les signalements des écoles et des hôpitaux, remontent un flot de violences intrafamiliales et une difficulté à « identifier les superpriorités parmi les superpriorités ».

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, G7 à Evian : après sa rencontre avec Donald Trump au G7, Voldymyr Zelensky rappelle qu’il « est toujours important que les Etats-Unis soient prêts à apporter leur soutien »
lemonde.description: Les domaines qui nécessitent ce soutien, selon le président ukrainien, sont l’augmentation du « nombre de missiles de défense aérienne » et la mise en place « d’un programme d’aide pour l’hiver »

lemonde.title: Le BHV Marais, à Paris, va interrompre son partenariat avec Shein à l’occasion d’un changement de propriétaire
lemonde.description: Frédéric Merlin a décidé de céder le fonds de commerce à une nouvelle structure, fondée par des cadres actuels de l’établissement. Cette annonce concerne aussi le BHV Parly 2 dans les Yvelines, mais pas les sept BHV de province (ex-Galeries Lafayette).

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : Donald Trump a dit à Benyamin Nétanyahou que la Syrie peut s’occuper du Hezbollah si Israël ne peut pas « le faire » sans faire de victimes civiles au Liban
lemonde.description: Le président américain a fait ces déclarations en marge du sommet du G7, affirmant avoir fait part de son mécontentement au premier ministre après les récentes frappes israéliennes sur Beyrouth et la banlieue sud de la capitale libanaise.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Les Ecologistes écartelés sur leur stratégie, au risque de devenir inaudibles
lemonde.description: A moins d’un an de l’élection, la stratégie du « trait d’union » de la gauche, impulsée par Marine Tondelier depuis 2024, place le parti Vert au second plan par rapport aux autres forces en présence.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : la presse espagnole acte l’« échec retentissant » de la Roja, accrochée par le Cap-Vert pour son entrée dans le Mondial
lemonde.description: Les joueurs de Luis de la Fuente, présentés comme favoris de la compétition, ont raté leurs débuts face aux Requins bleus du Cap-Vert, lundi 15 juin, en concédant le match nul (0-0). Un résultat jugé sévèrement de l’autre côté des Pyrénées.

lemonde.title: A la Fed, premier dilemme pour Kevin Warsh : baisser les taux pour contenter Donald Trump, ou les relever pour tenter de contenir l’inflation
lemonde.description: Le nouveau président de la banque centrale américaine est confronté à l’accélération de la hausse des prix liée au conflit au Moyen-Orient, alors que le président l’a choisi en espérant qu’il baisserait les taux d’intérêt.

lemonde.title: En France, les émissions de CO₂ en 2024 et en 2025 ont baissé plus qu’anticipé
lemonde.description: Le Citepa a rapporté que les émissions de gaz à effet de serre ont baissé de 3 % en 2024 et de 2,1 % l’année suivante, alors que la dernière estimation envisageait plutôt des baisses de l’ordre de 1,8 % et de 1,5 %.

lemonde.title: Eric Ciotti accuse le ministre des transports, Philippe Tabarot, de l’avoir menacé, et demande son exclusion du gouvernement
lemonde.description: Le maire de Nice a adressé un courrier au premier ministre, dans lequel il dénonce des comportements d’« une gravité exceptionnelle » en marge d’un événement au Palais des congrès de Nice, dimanche.

lemonde.title: Convoqué devant la justice pour « harcèlement » des bénéficiaires du RSA, le président du Finistère défend sa politique de contrôle
lemonde.description: Devant le tribunal de Brest, six allocataires du RSA, la CGT et la Confédération paysanne ont dénoncé la « traque aux précaires » de Maël de Calan. Dénonçant un « procès politique », la figure montante de la droite bretonne se félicite d’avoir diminué le nombre de bénéficiaires du RSA de 18 000 à 13 500.

lemonde.title: En Hongrie, le premier ministre Péter Magyar peine à obtenir le départ des caciques de l’ère Viktor Orban
lemonde.description: Le symbole de la résistance opposée par les responsables de l’ancienne majorité est le président Tamas Sulyok, qui refuse de donner sa démission en dépit de l’ultimatum que lui avait fixé le chef de gouvernement.

lemonde.title: Au Royaume-Uni, l’ancienne cité minière de Dudley confrontée à la « génération perdue » de ses jeunes ni en études, ni en emploi, ni en formation
lemonde.description: Plus de 1 million de jeunes Britanniques sont inactifs, un chiffre en hausse lié aux défaillances du système d’éducation, à l’augmentation des problèmes médicaux et à la désindustrialisation de certaines régions. A Dudley, dans le centre de l’Angleterre, une personne âgée de 16 à 24 ans sur cinq est dans ce cas.

lemonde.title: En Suède, un homme condamné à quatre ans de prison pour avoir forcé son épouse à se prostituer auprès d’une centaine d’hommes
lemonde.description: L’homme a été reconnu coupable de proxénétisme aggravé ainsi que de tentative de viol, agression et menaces pour des faits qui se sont étalés sur plus de trois ans, selon un communiqué du tribunal.

lemonde.title: « En rachetant Roku, l’empire américain de médias Fox vise à rattraper son retard en matière de streaming »
lemonde.description: Le groupe de la famille Murdoch a annoncé, lundi, qu’il allait acquérir, pour 22 milliards de dollars, le fabricant de boîtiers de téléviseurs, présent dans 100 millions de foyers américains, relève Isabelle Chaperon, chroniqueuse au service Economie du « Monde ».

lemonde.title: « Donald Trump pense prendre Cuba par la force ou l’usure, mais oublie que le parti unique conserve son rôle régulateur »
lemonde.description: Le sociologue Vincent Bloch analyse, dans une tribune au « Monde », les logiques derrière la prédation économique et politique qu’affiche l’administration américaine vis-à-vis du régime cubain.

lemonde.title: Naufrage dans la Manche en 2021 : procès ordonné pour 14 membres de réseaux de passeurs
lemonde.description: Ils sont poursuivis notamment pour homicides involontaires, blessures involontaires, aide au séjour irrégulier en bande organisée et participation a une association de malfaiteurs, a précisé le Parquet national anticriminalité organisé.

france24fr.title: Le G7 fait monter la pression sur Poutine pour arrêter la guerre avec l'Ukraine
france24fr.description: Réunis au G7 en présence du président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky, les dirigeants des grandes puissances ont affiché leur volonté de renforcer la pression sur Moscou pour arrêter la guerre en Ukraine. Même Donald Trump assure désormais vouloir faire "tout ce qu’il peut" pour forcer la main de la Russie.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : 50 ans après le soulèvement de Soweto, le devoir de mémoire
france24fr.description: À l’occasion du 50ᵉ anniversaire du soulèvement du 16 juin 1976, qui a marqué un tournant décisif dans la lutte contre l’apartheid en Afrique du Sud, Soweto porte aujourd’hui peu de traces visibles des violences qui s’y sont déroulées.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la clé Deschamps ? Parlons-en avec T. M'Bo, D. Rouch, R. Molina et A. Dupuis
france24fr.description: Didier Deschamps, le sélectionneur des Bleus, a passé quarante ans dans le football - onze en équipe de France et quatorze à la tête de l'équipe de France. C'est son dernier Mondial et ses derniers matchs avec les tricolores.

france24fr.title: Zelensky est arrivé au sommet du G7 en France
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky est arrivé mardi matin au sommet du G7 à Evian, en France, durant lequel six des sept dirigeants de ce club de pays industrialisés espèrent convaincre Donald Trump de soutenir davantage l'Ukraine face à la Russie, ont constaté des journalistes de l'AFP.

france24fr.title: Iran/États-Unis : le protocole d'accord est "un accord équitable", selon Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a déclaré mardi que le protocole ⁠d'accord visant à mettre ​fin à la guerre entre l'Iran et les Etats-Unis était un "accord équitable" et répété que l'accord définitif, qui doit encore être négocié, garantirait que Téhéran ne ​pourra jamais se doter de l'arme atomique.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : Costinha analyse les Bleus avant le choc contre le Sénégal
france24fr.description: À quelques heures de France-Sénégal, Costinha, ancien milieu de terrain du Portugal et ex-international, revient sur les forces de l’équipe de France au Mondial 2026, le débat autour de son animation offensive et le statut de favori des Bleus dans la compétition.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : les Bleus entrent en lice contre le Sénégal
france24fr.description: C'est le "D-Day" dans le New Jersey pour les Bleus, en quête d'une troisième étoile, et qui vont faire leurs débuts dans le tournoi à 21h00 (15h00 locale) avec des retrouvailles corsées face aux Sénégalais qui les avaient battus en ouverture de l'édition 2002.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : France 24 à New York pour couvrir le premier match des Bleus
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France, emmenée par sa ligne d'attaque magique Mbappé-Dembélé-Olise, débute son aventure au Mondial-2026 en se frottant au Sénégal. Pour l’occasion, les envoyés spéciaux de France 24 ont fait le déplacement à New York.

france24fr.title: Dans la Syrie post-Assad, les déplacés attendent la reconstruction
france24fr.description: La Syrie est particulièrement impactée par la baisse de l’aide humanitaire mondiale, notamment américaine. Dans le nord-ouest du pays, des centaines de milliers de déplacés vivent toujours dans des abris de fortune. A la chute du régime, ils espéraient pouvoir rentrer chez eux. Mais en voyant leurs villages détruits, la plupart sont restés coincés dans des camps en attendant une reconstruction qui prendra des années. A mesure que le temps passe, les conditions de vie s’y dégradent et les infrast

france24fr.title: IA : le choc Anthropic relance la bataille de la souveraineté
france24fr.description: L’interdiction d’accès aux modèles les plus avancés d’Anthropic a créé une onde de choc en Europe. Alors que Paris annonce 655 millions d’euros supplémentaires pour l’intelligence artificielle. L’épisode rappelle la dépendance du continent aux technologies américaines.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Bleus ouvrent leur compétition face au Sénégal
france24fr.description: L’équipe de France fait son entrée en lice dans la Coupe du monde face au Sénégal. Les Bleus veulent éviter un remake du match d’ouverture de la Coupe du monde 2002 (défaite 1-0).

france24fr.title: L'Iran, l'équipe "la plus maltraitée" du Mondial selon son sélectionneur
france24fr.description: L'entraîneur iranien Amir Ghalenoei a déclaré lundi que son équipe était "maltraitée" en raison de changements à la dernière minute dans les horaires de voyage, dus aux tensions entre l'Iran et les États-Unis. D'après lui, ces mauvaises conditions ont affecté les performances de ses joueurs qui n'ont récolté qu'un match nul 2-2 contre la Nouvelle-Zélande.

france24fr.title: Le gardien capverdien Vozinha, héros inattendu du début du Mondial 2026
france24fr.description: Les Coupes du monde sont souvent le théâtre d’histoires extraordinaires, et l’édition 2026 tient déjà la sienne. Celle de Vozinha, le gardien du Cap-Vert, qui a largement contribué à l’exploit retentissant lundi de sa sélection face à l’Espagne (0-0). À 40 ans, pour sa première apparition dans la compétition, il s’est érigé en héros d’un résultat historique pour son pays.

france24fr.title: IA : la France va investir 655 millions d'euros supplémentaires pour accélérer sa "révolution"
france24fr.description: À la veille de l'ouverture du salon VivaTech, dédié aux nouvelles technologies, à Paris, le Premier ministre a annoncé mardi un investissement supplémentaire de 655 millions d'euros dans l’intelligence artificielle. Ces fonds doivent notamment renforcer les infrastructures, la recherche, les entreprises et les filières industrielles". L'objectif affiché est de soutenir la souveraineté technologique française et moderniser les services publics, afin "que cette révolution profite aux Français".

france24fr.title: France-Sénégal 2002 : le jour où les Lions de la Teranga ont fait tomber les champions du monde
france24fr.description: Pour la deuxième fois de leur histoire, la France et le Sénégal vont s'affronter mardi en Coupe du monde. Il y a 24 ans, les Lions de la Teranga avaient créé la sensation en Corée du Sud en battant les Bleus, champions du monde et d'Europe en titre.

france24fr.title: Accord entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran : "Trump nous a trahis"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mardi 16 juin, la suite des réactions, aux Etats-Unis, à l’accord entre Washington et Téhéran pour mettre fin à la guerre en Iran. Un accord accueilli avec inquiétude au Liban et en Iran. Le combat d’une Franco-vietnamienne contre les multinationales responsables de l’épandage d’agent orange pendant la guerre du Vietnam. Le bel exploit du Cap-Vert face à l’Espagne au Mondial. Et la mobilisation en faveur de Christophe Gleizes.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Iran et Nouvelle-Zélande font match nul, bataille des symboles en tribunes
france24fr.description: Les équipes d'Iran et de Nouvelle-Zélande se sont neutralisées (2-2) lors de leur entrée en lice dans la Coupe du monde, lundi à Los Angeles. Des membres de la diaspora iranienne ont manifesté devant le stade, et de nombreux drapeaux ornés du lion et du soleil - symboles du drapeau avant la révolution de 1979 - ont été brandis dans les tribunes, notamment pendant l'hymne, en partie hué, avant que le public n'apporte un bruyant soutien aux joueurs.

france24fr.title: Antonio Guterres en visite de "solidarité" en Haïti
france24fr.description: Le secrétaire général de l'ONU Antonio Guterres est attendu mardi en Haïti pour exprimer sa "solidarité" avec les souffrances de la population. Plus de 5 000 personnes ont trouvé la mort en un an, victimes des violences liées aux gangs.

zeit.description: Das Europaparlament findet einen Veggie-Kompromiss: Bezeichnungen wie »Veggie-Burger«, »-Wurst« und »-Nuggets« sind erlaubt. »Veggie-Speck« soll verboten werden.

zeit.description: Die Zollvereinbarung zwischen den USA und der EU hat eine wichtige Hürde genommen: Das EU-Parlament stimmte für den Deal. Nun muss noch der Rat der EU-Länder zustimmen.

nzz.description: In Deutschland und der Schweiz ist es immer schwieriger, die Fahrprüfung zu bestehen. Die bürokratischen und monetären Hürden sind hoch. Gleichzeitig arbeitet die Autoindustrie an der Abschaffung des menschlichen Fahrers. Es wird Zeit, sich an neue Gegebenheiten anzupassen.

nzz.description: Der Turnierfavorit Spanien erreicht nur ein Unentschieden gegen den kleinen Inselstaat. Ist das ein Ausrutscher oder ein Vorbote tiefer liegender Probleme?

nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Polizei führt Razzien gegen Opposition in Istanbul durch
spiegel.description: Im Fokus der türkischen Justiz ist dieses Mal der Bezirk von Ex-Bürgermeister Ekrem İmamoğlu. Bei Baufirmen und in Verwaltungen werden 27 Personen festgenommen. Die Razzien folgen einem bekannten Muster.

spiegel.title: G7: Merz umschmeichelt Trump
spiegel.description: Die Europäer versuchen beim G7-Gipfel in Évian, den US-Präsidenten mit Schmeicheleien bei Laune zu halten. Und plötzlich keimt Hoffnung bei einem Thema auf, das Trump zuletzt kaum noch interessierte.

spiegel.title: Wetter in Deutschland: Hitzewelle für einige Landesteile erwartet
spiegel.description: Bis zu 36 Grad am Oberrhein: Der Deutsche Wetterdienst erwartet eine Hitzewelle für einige Landesteile. Selbst nachts werden mancherorts die Temperaturen wohl nicht unter 20 Grad sinken.

spiegel.title: Tennis: Serena und Venus Williams spielen noch ein Doppel in Wimbledon
spiegel.description: Gerade ist Serena Williams wieder auf die große Tennis-Bühne zurückgekehrt, nun tritt sie gemeinsam mit ihrer Schwester in Wimbledon an. Spekuliert wird auch über einen Start im Einzel, eine Wildcard ist noch offen.

spiegel.title: AfD: Wie die etablierten Parteien den Rechten das Geschäft erleichtern - Meinung
spiegel.description: Der Aufstieg der AfD scheint unaufhaltsam. Das liegt auch an einem Dilemma, in das sich Union, SPD und Co. selbst hineinmanövriert haben.

spiegel.title: VW-Konzern: Volkswagen-Bosse halten Konzern laut Recherche für existenzgefährdet
spiegel.description: Eine anonyme Umfrage unter Vorständen und Aufsichtsräten sollte bei Volkswagen die Lage erfassen. Laut manager magazin zeigt sich: Die Spitzenleute fürchten um die Zukunft – und attestieren sich selbst Uneinigkeit.

spiegel.title: Europaparlament: Die Veggiewurst darf ihren Namen behalten
spiegel.description: Sojaschnitzel und Veggieburger dürfen weiter so heißen. Das hat das EU-Parlament entschieden. Für bestimmte Ersatzprodukte gilt aber weiter ein Namensverbot.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Fan-Proteste rund um Irans erstes Gruppenspiel
spiegel.description: Die Fifa wollte Sport und Politik bei der WM trennen. Das erste Gruppenspiel der Iraner zeigte: Das ist nicht so einfach. Manche zahlen Hunderte Dollar für eine Karte, um die Spieler zu stören.

spiegel.title: Bakterien und Viren: Menschen im gleichen Haushalt teilen sich viele Mikroben im Körper
spiegel.description: Die Mikroorganismen im Körper ähneln sich bei Menschen im selben Haushalt – egal, ob es sich um Geschwister, Eltern und Kinder oder um WG-Mitbewohner handelt. Paare weisen besonders starke Gemeinsamkeiten auf.

spiegel.title: Fußball: Innenministerkonferenz zaudert bei Maßnahmen gegen Pyro-Technik in Stadien
spiegel.description: Es geht um die hässliche Seite des Fußballs: Die Innenminister diskutieren in Hamburg über Krawalle, Pyroattacken, Hassplakate. Doch vor allem im Kampf gegen das gefährliche Feuerwerk sind die Länder nicht einig.

spiegel.title: Zölle: Europaparlament beschließt Umsetzung des Handelsdeals mit den USA
spiegel.description: Das Europaparlament hat im Zollstreit mit den USA das Ergebnis der Verhandlungen mit den Mitgliedstaaten und der EU-Kommission gebilligt. Damit dürften europäische Zölle auf US-Industriewaren schon bald fallen.

spiegel.title: Wegen Belfast-Berichterstattung: Elon Musk geht rechtlich gegen ZDF vor
spiegel.description: Das ZDF hatte in einem Bericht suggeriert, der Techunternehmer Elon Musk habe dazu aufgerufen, in Belfast »Jagd auf Migranten« zu machen. Nun schickte sein Anwalt eine Abmahnung - der Sender entfernte die entsprechende Passage.

spiegel.title: Telegram: Indien schränkt Zugang zum Messaging-Dienst ein
spiegel.description: Telegram ist in Indien ein wichtiger Kommunikationskanal – und ein Umschlagplatz für angebliche Prüfungsdokumente. Staatliche Sperrmaßnahmen sollen jetzt Studienbewerber vor Betrug schützen.

spiegel.title: Mehmet Scholl: Mann soll in das Haus eingedrungen sein – und sich ins Bett der Tochter gelegt haben
spiegel.description: Ein 48-Jähriger soll in das Haus von Ex-Fußballer Mehmet Scholl eingestiegen sein und sich unbekleidet in das Bett seiner Tochter gelegt haben. Der Verdächtige wurde offenbar von der 20-Jährigen und ihrem Freund überwältigt.

spiegel.title: Augsburg: Polizist wegen Bestechung eines TÜV-Prüfers zu 7800 Euro Geldstrafe verurteilt
spiegel.description: Ein Polizist wollte beim TÜV offenbar Zeit sparen – und griff zu illegalen Mitteln. Nun ist der Mann verurteilt worden, kam aber eher glimpflich davon.

spiegel.title: Inflation bei Lebensmitteln: Deutsche Haushalte gaben 2023 im Schnitt 335 Euro pro Monat aus
spiegel.description: Lebensmittel sind in den vergangenen Jahren besonders teuer geworden, ihr Anteil an den privaten Konsumausgaben ist aber erstaunlich stabil. Besonders viel Geld fließt für Fleisch und Fisch.

new-sci.description: The outer solar system once seemed like a quiet backwater. But a glut of tiny, strange moons with unruly orbits are coming into view, revealing hints of a surprising past – and the origin of Saturn's rings

new-sci.description: A visit to Kew Gardens’ exhibit of the sculptor’s work is a fascinating insight into how he was inspired by nature

new-sci.title: Striking photos show how sands are encroaching on oases in the Sahara
new-sci.description: A photo essay from Tommy Trenchard explores efforts to protect the fragile ecosystems of oases in Chad

phys-org.title: Back from the brink: Bettongs return to the desert
phys-org.description: Researchers are celebrating the release of the once locally extinct burrowing bettong back into the NSW desert—with the aim of training them to survive alongside feral cats and foxes.

phys-org.title: Young disk around WRAY 15-1880 may contain a primitive planetary system
phys-org.description: Italian astronomers have used the Very Large Telescope (VLT) to perform polarimetric observations of the star WRAY 15-1880 and its young circumstellar disk. Results of the new observations, presented June 10 on the arXiv preprint server, suggest that this disk may host a primitive planetary system.

phys-org.title: New alliance to protect Atlantic's leatherback turtles launched on World Sea Turtle Day
phys-org.description: A newly established alliance, comprising leading researchers and conservation experts, has mobilized to safeguard the Atlantic Ocean's leatherback turtle populations. The Wilkes Atlantic Leatherback Turtle Alliance is led by the University of Exeter, with more than 50 partner organizations in 25 countries around the Atlantic.

phys-org.title: New tool helps protect communities from flooding during rain-on-snow events and optimize reservoir management
phys-org.description: While Reno families were celebrating the 1997 New Year, the Truckee River was surging into the city's downtown streets. A rainstorm was falling on the Sierra Nevada's deep snowpack, melting it rapidly and creating a hazardous situation for downstream communities.

phys-org.title: Jury service boosts public trust in courts, but fewer Americans are serving
phys-org.description: As public trust in the U.S. Supreme Court continues to fall, new research from the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) of the University of Pennsylvania finds that jury service is associated with more positive attitudes toward courts and judges—but that Americans' opportunities to serve are shrinking as jury trials become increasingly rare.

phys-org.title: New research suggests writing with AI demands more thought from students, not less
phys-org.description: Writing with AI can look deceptively simple. Effortless, even. Type in a prompt and a polished paragraph appears in seconds. Tidy, confident, clean. But that apparent ease is also deceiving, says Abram Anders, associate professor of English and the Jonathan Wickert Professor of Innovation at Iowa State University.

phys-org.title: Powerful UFO spotted blasting from a distant black hole
phys-org.description: Astronomers have detected one of the most powerful ultra-fast outflows ever seen from a distant supermassive black hole. Using XMM-Newton and NuSTAR, a team studied a hyper-luminous quasar at cosmic noon and found two distinct wind components blasting away from the black hole, details of which are outlined in a paper submitted to the arXiv preprint server on June 3. The study has been submitted to the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics and is currently under minor revision.

phys-org.title: Experts probe 'shock' arrival of mosquito virus in Scotland
phys-org.description: It was something infectious disease expert Heather Ferguson never expected to see in her lifetime: a mosquito-borne virus originally from Africa spreading in Scotland.

phys-org.title: Scaling up key as French firm bets on sterile mosquitoes
phys-org.description: Inside a factory in southern France, millions of tiger mosquitoes are being bred, not to spread, but to stop them from reproducing—though scaling up such efforts poses a mighty challenge.

phys-org.title: SpaceX shares skyrocket as money raised hits $85.7 billion
phys-org.description: SpaceX shares shot 20% higher Monday as the company said it raised a record-breaking $85.7 billion.

phys-org.title: Mongooses prepare for likely future battles with powerful enemies, study finds
phys-org.description: Dwarf mongooses anticipate encounters with rival groups and adjust how they move, communicate and defend resources beforehand, according to new research from the University of Bristol. The study, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, shows that mongoose groups alter their behavior in areas where fights with rivals are most likely, even in the absence of another group. The biggest changes occur when the anticipated threat is greatest.

phys-org.title: Argentine mining threatens scarce water resources in the Andes
phys-org.description: San Juan's once-sparkling rivers have shriveled due to drought, and residents in the rugged, western Argentine province fear that prospective mining projects in the Andes will make matters worse.

phys-org.title: Toxic 'time bomb' threatens Mekong river basin
phys-org.description: Thai fisherman Somdet Singthong steered his metal skiff across the brown waters of the Mekong River, resigned to the pollution that has put his health and lifelong source of livelihood at risk.

phys-org.title: Global map reveals one-third of coral reefs may resist climate shocks
phys-org.description: In the crystalline waters off Kenya's coast, coral reefs are thriving—evidence of a rare good-news story in the battle to protect oceans from the ravages of climate change.

phys-org.title: 50-megapixel Earth models capture storms in unprecedented detail—but four consistent blind spots remain
phys-org.description: Traditional global climate models were like early digital cameras—they had only about 10,000 pixels to cover the entire planet. At that low resolution, big storm systems looked like blurry blobs. You couldn't see their true shape, how long they lasted or where they dumped the heaviest rain.

phys-org.title: Scientist confronting the rising global threat of mosquitoes
phys-org.description: Growing up in Tahiti, Anna-Bella Failloux saw firsthand the threat posed by mosquitoes: Nearly a third of adults on the picturesque island once had swollen limbs from elephantiasis caused by their bites.

phys-org.title: UK bans under-16s from using social media apps including TikTok and YouTube
phys-org.description: Britain will ban children aged under 16 from using a range of social media apps, including Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube, to protect them from harmful content and excessive screen time, Prime Minister Keir Starmer said Monday.

phys-org.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake shakes part of Indonesia, causing scattered damage
phys-org.description: A 6.7 magnitude earthquake shook part of central Indonesia's Sulawesi island Tuesday, causing scattered damage and rattling residents of a city devastated by a quake and tsunami eight years ago.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

proj-syn.title: Every British Prime Minister’s Nightmare
proj-syn.description: The true nature of Britain’s “special relationship” with the United States has far more to do with American financiers’ willingness to keep borrowing to purchase British government debt than with history, culture, or Britain’s defense needs. Every UK Prime Minister must bear this burden, which is rapidly becoming unsustainable.

proj-syn.title: India’s Unfinished Reform Agenda
proj-syn.description: Elevated oil prices, potentially strong El Niño conditions during the monsoon season, and the tariff-induced fragmentation of global trade are bearing down on the Indian economy and will likely be a drag on GDP growth. But these adverse conditions may be a blessing in disguise if they force India to complete its economic reform agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Middle East’s New Normal
proj-syn.description: The most likely outcome of the Iran war is not peace but an unsatisfying ceasefire that leaves the underlying issues unresolved. This will mean an uneasy equilibrium in which Gulf countries go their own way, US influence wanes, and the regional order remains unsettled.

proj-syn.title: No Bridge Over Healing Waters for the G7
proj-syn.description: The French G7 presidency’s focus on global imbalances is both welcome and problematic. While long-standing trade imbalances between the United States, Europe, and China are, if anything, becoming even more troublesome, the leaders’ summit in Évian-les-Bains will do nothing to address the problem.

proj-syn.title: Are Government Stakes the Key to AI Sovereignty?
proj-syn.description: At first glance, reports that the US and Chinese governments are both considering taking stakes in national AI champions would seem to suggest a convergence between the world’s two leading AI powers. But a closer look reveals stark differences in their underlying strategies.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: Jefferson’s Revolutionary Language
proj-syn.description: Of the delegates who assembled in Philadelphia in 1776 for the Second Continental Congress, only Thomas Jefferson possessed the skill, knowledge, and linguistic gifts to make the Declaration of Independence an immortal text. He was the self-appointed conscience of America, and sensational imagery was his stock-in-trade.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of the Enslaved
proj-syn.description: For African-Americans, the Declaration of Independence was nothing but a “thin veil to cover the crimes” of slavery, as Frederick Douglass put it. Inspired by Haiti’s Declaration of Independence, free and enslaved Black people in the US found themselves subverting America’s founding document to achieve their own emancipation.

proj-syn.title: Free-Market Capitalism Is Destroying US Democracy
proj-syn.description: Far from two sides of the same coin, free-market capitalism and democracy are fundamentally incompatible. The only way to restore US democracy is to transform the system, so that it compensates innovators but limits their market power, while ensuring that the benefits of economic progress are more equitably shared.

proj-syn.title: Canada’s Great Recalibration
proj-syn.description: The growing fusion of economics, security, and technology has altered the nature of 21st-century interdependence, and Canada has responded by being more intentional. Rather than automatically serving as an extension of US-centered systems, it is creating more options across a wider network of relationships.

proj-syn.title: From Jefferson to Nehru
proj-syn.description: The Declaration of Independence continues to challenge countries, including the US and India, to measure themselves against the ideals they profess. But in a century marked by rising inequality, an authoritarian resurgence, and the emergence of new forms of domination, measuring up will become only more difficult.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Democratic Decline
proj-syn.description: Notwithstanding recent setbacks for illiberal, populist, and authoritarian leaders in some countries, good-governance groups and experts on democratic decline continue to document a disturbing global trend toward “autocratization.” What remains to be seen is whether enough voters will wake up to the threat.

proj-syn.title: The Standard of Independence
proj-syn.description: Although revolutions would surely have occurred had the United States never broken from Britain in 1776, the Declaration of Independence gave later anticolonial movements inspiration and the language to shape their own aspirations. It offered a universal blueprint, even as the US itself adopted the ethos of empire.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of Independence Turns South
proj-syn.description: Whether they were agreeing or arguing, the new countries that emerged across the Americas after the American Revolution influenced each other. Together, they helped shape the global development of modern democracy and the social and political movements that have shaped it ever since.

proj-syn.title: Capitalism’s Creature
proj-syn.description: The American Dream, with its basis in Thomas Jefferson’s immortal words, was one of the most powerfully generative ideas ever conceived. But the economy and impersonal systems it helped to bring into being are now shaping society and its individual members, rather than the other way around.

proj-syn.title: What the Declaration Did and Did Not Say
proj-syn.description: The American founders’ understanding of political community was ethnically and racially restrictive in ways that Americans have since repudiated. But the Declaration of Independence’s underlying logic and treatment of rights and what it takes to secure them remains as cogent as it was 250 years ago.

proj-syn.title: Independence for Me, But Not for Thee
proj-syn.description: The Declaration of Independence spoke of all states as being "separate and equal," reflecting the founders' deference to the norms of international law and practice. Yet 250 years later, Donald Trump's administration has inverted this posture, much to the detriment of America's standing in the world.
